newsitem.title: USA: Big rise in Japan trade surplus unlikely-Hashimoto.
newsitem.headline: Big rise in Japan trade surplus unlikely-Hashimoto.

text.p: Japan's trade surplus is unlikely to rise siginficantly in the medium term, said Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
"I do not think that Japan's trade and services surplus will increase significantly," Hashimoto told reporters after the conclusion of the Group of Seven summit here.
G7 officials during the summit issued a joint statement saying Japan's objective was to avoid a significant increase in its trade surplus.
Hashimoto declined to address the impact of current foreign exchange rates on the efforts to limit Japan's surplus, but added that Japan will not accept wild swings in the yen's exchange rate.

"Even if the yen strengthens or the yen weakens relatively, we will not be able to accept and tolerate extreme changes in exchange rates. If exchange rates shift around extremely, that is not something we can tolerate," Hashimoto added.
